name: Maximum-Generated Classes and Conjunction Substitution
statement: Replacing one coordinate by conjunction of two fresh coordinates preserves and reflects membership in $\mathsf{MaxMin}$. A supplied rank-$r$ parent with $m$ auxiliaries yields a rank-$(r+1)$ parent with at most $m+1$ auxiliaries, and finite minimum parent rank satisfies $h(C)\le h(C^\wedge)\le h(C)+1$.
proof: Two rank-one control fibers have marked sections equal to the three-word conjunction-zero fiber and the singleton conjunction-one fiber. Insert them into a level-sum parent with the fiber-replacement theorem; the unique old heights are constant on the required components. Fixing one new input to one recovers the original class as a section, proving reflection and the lower rank bound.
